answer.text: IP3 and DAG, and IP3 releases calcium from the smooth endoplasmic reticulum
answer.line: Phospholipase C splits PIP2 into DAG, which stays in the membrane, and IP3, which travels to the smooth ER and lets calcium out.

steps: Name the cut. Phospholipase C splits the membrane lipid PIP2 into two pieces: IP3 and DAG.
Sort them by solubility. DAG is fatty and stays in the membrane; IP3 is water soluble and drifts through the cytosol.
IP3 opens calcium channels on the smooth ER, and the calcium drives smooth muscle contraction.

choices.text: cAMP and cGMP, and cAMP activates protein kinase A in the cytoplasm of the cell
choices.note: cAMP and cGMP come from the two cyclases, not phospholipase C. The protein kinase A link is real, but it belongs to the cAMP pathway.

choices.text: IP3 and DAG, and IP3 stays in the membrane to activate protein kinase C
choices.note: The pair is right, but the roles are swapped. DAG stays in the membrane for protein kinase C; IP3 is the one that travels.

choices.text: DAG and calcium, and DAG travels to the nucleus to bind DNA
choices.note: DAG is one product, but calcium is released later, not made by the cut. DAG stays in the membrane; it does not bind DNA.

choices.text: IP3 and DAG, and IP3 releases calcium from the smooth endoplasmic reticulum
choices.note: Water-soluble IP3 travels to the smooth ER and lets the calcium out.

choices.text: cAMP and calcium, and cAMP opens calcium channels in the nucleus
choices.note: cAMP comes from adenylyl cyclase, not phospholipase C. The calcium store IP3 opens is the ER, not the nucleus.

visual.reuse: new: the bio.diagram pathway layout with a membrane band
visual.alt: A slice of membrane with the outside above and the cytosol below. A hormone's receptor turns on phospholipase C, which cuts PIP2 into DAG, staying in the membrane to switch on protein kinase C, and IP3, which travels down to the smooth ER. The ER's calcium channels open, outlined as the answer, and calcium floods the cytosol.
visual.caption: Watch which piece leaves the membrane. DAG stays put; IP3 travels to the ER.
